title: MMVY Medhavi Scholarship 2026: Full Fees, ₹6L Income Rule
meta_description: MMVY 2026: MP students with 70% (MP Board) or 85% (CBSE) get full college fees paid. Income under ₹6 lakh, Samagra ID needed. Apply on medhavikalyan.mp.gov.in.

hero.one_liner: MP pays your full college tuition if you scored 70% in MP Board or 85% in CBSE and your family earns under ₹6 lakh.

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Medhavi Vidyarthi Yojana (MMVY) is Madhya Pradesh's flagship scholarship for students who score high in Class 12 but cannot afford college. The state pays your tuition fees directly, so your seat does not depend on your family's bank balance.

It covers engineering, medical, law, and regular graduation courses in recognised institutions across India, including IITs, IIMs, NLUs, and AIIMS. Over 1.5 lakh students have used it since 2017, with more than ₹500 crore disbursed.
The scheme runs on the Samagra ID system. You apply once online, your college verifies the claim, and the money goes to the institution or your Aadhaar-seeded account.

For a family earning ₹4-5 lakh a year, the difference is stark. An MBBS seat that would cost ₹40-50 lakh over the course becomes reachable, and an engineering degree costs at most the hostel and mess bills.

eligibility.label: Who can apply
eligibility.value: Permanent residents of Madhya Pradesh who passed Class 12 with 70% or more from MP Board, or 85% or more from CBSE/ICSE.

eligibility.label: Income limit
eligibility.value: Family income from all sources must be under ₹6 lakh per year. A relaxation up to ₹8 lakh for SC/ST students in select professional courses was reported in the 2026 state budget, confirm on the portal.

eligibility.label: Course requirement
eligibility.value: First-year admission in a recognised undergraduate course. Engineering needs JEE Main rank up to 1,50,000, medical needs NEET, law needs CLAT or the institute's exam.

eligibility.label: Mandatory IDs
eligibility.value: A valid 9-digit Samagra ID and Aadhaar are compulsory. Bank account should be Aadhaar-seeded for DBT.

eligibility.label: Where you can study
eligibility.value: Any recognised institution in India qualifies, including IITs, IIMs, NLUs, and AIIMS. Your domicile must be MP, your college does not have to be.

extra_sections.title: 📌 MMVY Status at a Glance (Verified 31 July 2026)
extra_sections.content:
Applications for the 2026-27 session run on medhavikalyan.mp.gov.in. The window typically opens with the admission season and stays open till late in the year, exact dates appear only on the portal.

Only apply on the official portal. No agent, no fee, no other website.

extra_sections.heading: Why MMVY Exists and Who It Actually Helps
content: Madhya Pradesh launched MMVY in 2017 after a simple observation. Thousands of students were clearing Class 12 with excellent marks and then dropping out because an engineering or medical seat costs more than their family earns in a year.
The scheme flips the problem. Instead of a small cash scholarship that covers books, MMVY takes over the biggest single expense, the tuition fee itself.

That is why the benefit is structured as fee payment rather than a fixed amount. A student in a ₹60,000 BSc course and a student in a ₹1.4 lakh engineering course both walk in free, because the state pays what the course actually charges.

The scheme sits under the Higher Education Department and runs fully online. There is no district quota, no interview, and no discretion involved, if you meet the criteria and your documents verify, the fee is sanctioned.

extra_sections.heading: The Marks Rule Explained: 70% vs 85%
content: The two different cutoffs confuse many families, so here is the logic. MP Board students need 70% because the board's marking runs tighter than CBSE.
CBSE and ICSE students need 85% under the same scheme. Both cutoffs apply to the Class 12 final result, not Class 10.
There is no relaxation in the percentage itself for any category. The category relaxation that exists is on the income side, not the marks side.

If you scored 69.8% in MP Board, the portal will reject the application at the validation step. There is no rounding up and no appeal route for marks, so know your exact percentage before you plan around this scheme.

extra_sections.title: What MMVY Does NOT Cover
extra_sections.content:
Hostel charges, mess fees, caution money, and personal expenses stay out of the scheme. Only tuition and admission fees are paid.

You also cannot stack MMVY with another major state or central scholarship for the same course. Pick the one that pays more for your situation.

extra_sections.heading: Budgeting the Part MMVY Will Not Pay
content: Plan the non-covered costs before you accept a seat, because they arrive every month while the scholarship pays once a year. Hostel and mess at a government engineering college typically run ₹4,000-8,000 per month depending on the city.

Private colleges often bundle transport, uniform, and activity charges that MMVY treats as personal expenses. Ask the accounts office for the full fee break-up in writing and mark which lines the scheme covers.
Caution money is refundable but payable upfront, usually ₹5,000-15,000. Keep it aside in the admission month so it never becomes the reason a confirmed seat slips.
Many MMVY students pair the scheme with a bank education loan only for living costs. That keeps the loan small, and the tuition, the expensive part, stays fully on the government.

extra_sections.heading: Getting the Samagra ID Right Before You Apply
content: The Samagra ID is MP's family database number, and MMVY treats it as the master record. When you enter the 9-digit ID, the portal pulls your name, family, and address from it automatically.

If you were born and schooled in MP, your family almost certainly has one already. Ask for the family's 8-digit ID and your personal 9-digit member ID, or search yourself on samagra.gov.in with your name and district.

Students whose families moved within MP often find their record stuck in the old district. Get it migrated at the Grama Panchayat or ward office before applying, because a mismatched address can stall college verification.
If any detail on Samagra differs from your Class 12 marksheet, correct Samagra first. The portal validates against the marksheet, and a spelling clash is a silent rejection waiting to happen.

extra_sections.heading: The Engineering Cap: How the ₹1.5 Lakh Math Works
content: Engineering has a cap that other courses do not, so run the numbers before choosing a college. If your private college charges ₹1.2 lakh per year, MMVY pays the full ₹1.2 lakh.
If the college charges ₹1.8 lakh, MMVY pays ₹1.5 lakh and the remaining ₹30,000 per year is yours. Over four years that gap becomes ₹1.2 lakh from your pocket.
Government college fees almost always sit below the cap, which makes them effectively free under the scheme. This is worth weighing when your JEE rank puts both options on the table.
Medical and law have no such cap. For MBBS in a private MP college, the scheme pays the full tuition and admission fee, which can run into several lakh per year.

extra_sections.heading: The Income Certificate: Where Applications Quietly Die
content: MMVY does not accept a self-declaration of income. You need a formal income certificate issued by the tehsildar or SDM office, and it must be current for the session you are applying in.
Apply for it on the MP e-District portal or at your Lok Seva Kendra with Aadhaar, Samagra ID, and a ration card or bank passbook. It usually arrives within a week or two.

The certificate must state family income from all sources, including agriculture and informal work. An understated certificate that clashes with visible records can get the scholarship recovered later, so keep it honest.
Renewals need a fresh certificate too if yours has expired. Calendar this for May-June each year so the document is ready before the renewal window.

extra_sections.heading: What Happens After You Submit
content: Submission is the halfway point, not the end. Your application lands in your college's MMVY queue, and the nodal officer there must log in and verify your admission and fee structure.
This college step is where most delays happen. Students assume the government is slow when the file has actually been sitting unverified at their own institute for weeks.

After verification, the department sanctions the amount and generates payment. The full chain from submission to money typically takes a few weeks to a couple of months depending on when in the session you applied.
Check the portal status weekly. The moment it reads Pending at Institute for more than two weeks, walk into the college office rather than waiting.

extra_sections.title: Renewal Rule Most Students Miss
extra_sections.content:
MMVY is not one-time. It renews every year of your course, but only if you clear each year and your college verifies you again.

Keep attendance above 75% and submit the renewal application every session. A missed renewal is the most common reason a final-year fee goes unpaid.

extra_sections.heading: MMVY vs Other Scholarships: Which One Should You Take
content: MP students usually qualify for more than one scheme, and the one-major-scholarship rule forces a choice. The comparison is simple: MMVY pays the fee, most others pay a stipend.

Post-matric scholarships for SC, ST, and OBC students pay maintenance amounts plus some fee components. For a low-fee BA or BSc course, post-matric can beat MMVY because the stipend exceeds the government-rate tuition.
For engineering, medical, and law, MMVY wins by a wide margin. No stipend scheme matches a ₹1.5 lakh yearly fee payment, let alone full MBBS tuition.

Gaon ki Beti and Pratibha Kiran are smaller MP schemes worth checking for rural and urban girls respectively. They pay monthly amounts and can sometimes combine with fee waivers, so read each scheme's stacking rule before deciding.

extra_sections.heading: Renewal Year by Year: Keeping the Money Flowing
content: First-year approval is not a four-year guarantee. Every academic year opens a renewal window, and every renewal needs three things: a passed result, college re-verification, and valid documents.
Failing a semester does not always end the scholarship, but a failed year does. The scheme funds the sanctioned course duration, so a year back means that year's fee is on you.
Course changes are the other trap. Switching college or branch mid-course requires the new institution to be approved and the change to be updated on the portal, otherwise payment stops silently.

Final-year students should verify their file status early in the session. A payment that shows Sanctioned but never generated is usually a bank seeding issue, and fixing it after convocation is far harder than before.

extra_sections.text: Your marks earned the seat. MMVY makes sure a fee receipt never takes it away.

extra_sections.heading: Common Rejection Reasons and How to Avoid Them
content: Income certificate mismatches cause the most rejections. The certificate must come from the tehsil, be recent, and state family income from all sources under the limit.
Samagra ID errors come second. If your Samagra record has a different name spelling or date of birth than your marksheet, fix the Samagra record first at your local body office, then apply.
Aadhaar seeding failures block the payment stage rather than the application. Your bank account must be linked to Aadhaar through NPCI mapping, not just KYC at the branch.
Finally, course mismatches. The college and course must be on the approved list on the portal, so confirm your exact course code there before paying any admission fee.

extra_sections.heading: The Entrance Exam Gate: JEE, NEET, and CLAT Rules
content: High board marks alone do not unlock professional courses under MMVY. Engineering admission must come through JEE Main with a rank up to 1,50,000, which keeps the scheme aimed at genuinely competitive students.

Medical seats need NEET qualification, since that is the only admission route to MBBS and BDS anyway. The scheme then covers even private MP medical college tuition, which is where it saves families the most.

Law students need CLAT for the NLUs or the institute's own entrance where applicable. Regular BA, BSc, BCom, nursing, and polytechnic admissions need no entrance, board marks and a recognised institution are enough.
Keep the scorecard PDF from the exam year safe. The portal asks for it during document upload, and a missing scorecard holds the file at the very first verification step.

faqs.question: MMVY scholarship kya hai aur kitna paisa milta hai?
faqs.answer:
MMVY Madhya Pradesh ki scholarship hai jo aapki college tuition fee bharti hai. Engineering mein full fee ya ₹1.5 lakh per year (jo kam ho), medical aur law mein poori tuition aur admission fee.

Baaki graduation courses mein government-rate tuition fee cover hoti hai.

faqs.question: What is the income limit for MMVY 2026?
faqs.answer:
Family income from all sources must be under ₹6 lakh per year. The 2026 state budget reportedly relaxed this to ₹8 lakh for SC/ST students in select professional courses.

Confirm the relaxed limit on medhavikalyan.mp.gov.in before relying on it.

faqs.question: MMVY ke liye kitne percent chahiye?
faqs.answer:
MP Board se Class 12 mein kam se kam 70% chahiye. CBSE ya ICSE se 85% chahiye.

Engineering ke liye JEE Main rank 1,50,000 tak honi chahiye, medical ke liye NEET aur law ke liye CLAT.

faqs.question: Is Samagra ID compulsory for MMVY?
faqs.answer:
Yes, the entire application runs on your 9-digit Samagra ID. The portal fetches your details from it at registration.

No Samagra ID means no application, so create or find yours at samagra.gov.in first.

faqs.question: Does MMVY cover hostel and mess fees?
faqs.answer:
No. Only tuition and admission fees are covered.

Hostel charges, mess fees, caution money, and personal expenses are yours to pay.

faqs.question: MMVY login kaise kare?
faqs.answer:
medhavikalyan.mp.gov.in kholiye aur Application tab mein Existing Applicant chuniye. Apna 9-digit Samagra ID, applicant ID aur password daaliye.

Password bhool gaye? Login page ke Forgot Password se Samagra ID ke saath reset ho jata hai.

faqs.question: MMVY status kaise check karein?
faqs.answer:
Log in to medhavikalyan.mp.gov.in and open your application. The status label shows the stage: Pending at Institute, Verified, Sanctioned, or Payment Generated.

Pending at Institute means your college has not verified yet, so meet the MMVY nodal officer there.

faqs.question: Can I take MMVY along with another scholarship?
faqs.answer:
Generally no, one major government scholarship per course is the rule. If your institution gives a fee waiver (not a scholarship), MMVY can still cover the remaining fee.

Compare payouts and pick the scheme that covers more for your course.

faqs.question: Is MMVY only for colleges inside Madhya Pradesh?
faqs.answer:
No. Recognised institutions across India qualify, including IITs, IIMs, NLUs, and AIIMS.

Your domicile must be MP, but your college can be anywhere in the country.

faqs.question: What happens to MMVY in second and third year?
faqs.answer:
The scholarship renews each year of the course if you pass and your college verifies you again. Keep attendance above 75%.

Submit the renewal application every session, a missed renewal is the most common reason a fee goes unpaid.
